messages:
maria: Heads-up — prod eu-west Helm/GitOps deploys started failing ~10m ago. CI render step errors on sops decryption during helmfile/helm render. CI run: https://ci.redwood.internal/run/9234

kevin: Seeing it too. GPU model-serving pods in eu-west are CrashLooping because env secrets never made it into the pods (init container failed).

maria: Log excerpt from the CI render step:
```
sops: decryption failed: gcpkms: key not found: projects/redwood-prod/locations/eu-west1/keyRings/sops/cryptoKeys/redwood-sops-key
```

sophie: We rotated KMS keys earlier today as part of the monthly rotation. The alias `redwood-sops-key` was re-pointed, but it looks like the new key landed in us-east1. The sops config in the infra repo references an env var that constructs the KMS resource — could be using the wrong region value.

ryan: Quick diagnosis: GitHub Actions runners build the kms resource from SOPS_KMS_RESOURCE env which was updated in infra@6f1e. That change used a cluster-agnostic alias (no explicit location) and the alias resolves to the most-recent key (us-east1). Decrypting for eu-west targets fails because KMS resource is region-scoped.

kevin: Because decryption failed, the GitOps pipeline skipped injecting encrypted secrets and fell back to a CPU-only chart for the affected release. That caused a capacity mismatch (we tried to route GPU load to CPU nodes) and latency/cost spike for the service.

maria: Proposed immediate mitigations:
- Re-point the alias back to the eu-west1 key (if possible) OR
- Re-encrypt the secret with an explicit eu-west1 key and push to gitops/secrets so the eu-west render succeeds
- Add a short CI validation that attempts to decrypt a sample secret for each target region before allowing the merge

sophie: I can open a hotfix to infra: change the `sops_kms_resource` to be an explicit per-cluster mapping in `helmfile.env` and add a `sops_decrypt_check` step in GH Actions. Also add a note in the rotation runbook to update the cluster->region matrix.

ryan: We should also add a smoke verification to rollout automation: after `helm upgrade --install`, assert that pods report the expected environment variable(s) and init container exit code == 0, otherwise trigger rollback. I'll prepare a quick PR.

maria: For fastest recovery I think re-encrypt+push for the eu-west secret is safest (avoids waiting on alias DNS/repoint). Can someone do that now?

kevin: I'll re-encrypt and push a temporary secret under `gitops/secrets/eu-west/` with the explicit kms resource. Command I used locally:
```bash
SOPS_KMS_RESOURCE=projects/redwood-prod/locations/eu-west1/keyRings/sops/cryptoKeys/redwood-sops-key \
  sops --encrypt --gcp-kms "\$SOPS_KMS_RESOURCE" -i secrets/model-service.yaml
```

deploy-bot: Rollback triggered: reverted infra@6f1e -> infra@6f1d (sops_kms_resource mapping). Deploy started.

ci-bot: CI render -> success for eu-west target (sops decryption OK). Helm release sync in progress.

sophie: :thumbsup: I'll follow up with PRs: 1) explicit per-region SOPS mapping, 2) CI decrypt smoke tests, 3) rotation runbook updates.

ryan: Filing an incident ticket with the postmortem checklist — main action items: prevent ambiguous alias use, add per-region decrypt tests, add rollout smoke-checks. Incident INC-2026.

maria: Thanks all. After this stabilizes we should audit the other regions (eu-central, us-west) to ensure their SOPS keys and pipeline mappings are explicit.
